courses.summary: Use spreadsheets with confidence: formulas, workbooks, pivot tables and what Excel can do.

lessons.title: Spreadsheets
lessons.why: Spreadsheets are still the most common data tool at work. Formulas and what-if analysis save hours of manual calculation.
lessons.try: Build a small budget with a total formula, then change one value and watch the total update.

lessons.title: Summarising with pivot tables
lessons.why: A pivot table summarises thousands of rows — totals by month, averages by team — in a few clicks.
lessons.try: Make a pivot table from a sales list that shows total sales per product.

lessons.title: Microsoft Excel
lessons.why: Excel adds charts, pivot tables and macros (VBA) that automate repetitive steps.
lessons.try: Record a simple macro that formats a table, then run it on a new sheet.

quiz.q: Spreadsheets were developed as computerised versions of…
quiz.explain: Spreadsheets began as computerised analogues of paper accounting worksheets.

quiz.q: Several worksheets gathered together in one file form a…
quiz.explain: Sheets are gathered together to form a workbook.

quiz.q: Why are spreadsheets useful for 'what-if' analysis?
options: You can change a value and immediately see the effect on calculated values
quiz.explain: Changing any stored value recalculates the results automatically.

quiz.q: A pivot table shows…
options: aggregations such as sums, averages or counts of groups from a larger table
quiz.explain: Pivot tables aggregate groups of values from a larger table.

quiz.q: Which macro programming language does Excel include?
quiz.explain: Excel includes the VBA macro language.

courses.summary: Build everyday digital skills: find and judge information, collaborate online and stay safe from scams.

lessons.title: Digital literacy
lessons.why: Digital literacy is the foundation for every other tech skill and for most jobs today.
lessons.try: Pick a news story and check it against two other trustworthy sources before sharing it.

lessons.title: Working together online
lessons.why: Shared documents and version history let a team work on one file without emailing copies back and forth.
lessons.try: Create a shared document, invite a colleague to edit it, and look at its version history together.

lessons.title: Spotting phishing
lessons.why: Phishing is one of the most common ways attackers get in. Spotting it protects you and your organisation.
lessons.try: Look at a suspicious message and list three warning signs: urgency, strange links, requests for passwords or codes.

quiz.q: Digital literacy is the ability to…
options: type faster than 100 words per minute
find, evaluate and communicate information using digital devices and platforms
quiz.explain: It means finding, evaluating, creating and communicating information digitally.

quiz.q: Which literacy focuses on analysing and interpreting media messages and their influence?
quiz.explain: Media literacy is about analysing media messages; digital literacy integrates it with practical digital skills.

quiz.q: Real-time collaborative editing platforms let several users…
options: edit a single file at the same time
quiz.explain: They allow live, simultaneous and reversible editing of a single file.

quiz.q: Phishing is…
options: a scam that deceives people into revealing sensitive information or installing malware
a way to back up files
quiz.explain: Phishing is a form of social engineering and a scam.

quiz.q: Phishing by SMS text message is called…
quiz.explain: SMS phishing is smishing; voice phishing is vishing.

courses.summary: See how software is built step by step, how Git tracks changes, and how web applications work.

lessons.title: How software gets built
lessons.why: Knowing how software is planned, built, tested and maintained helps you work well on any tech team.
lessons.try: Write the steps from an idea to a released app, from requirements to maintenance.

lessons.title: Version control with Git
lessons.why: Git keeps every version of your work, so a team can work in parallel and undo mistakes safely.
lessons.try: Create a free GitHub account and make your first repository with a README file.

lessons.title: Web applications
lessons.why: Most business software now runs in the browser. Web skills let you build tools anyone can open with a link.
lessons.try: Open your browser's developer tools on any website and inspect the HTML of one element on the page.

quiz.q: A software development process typically…
options: divides the overall effort into smaller steps to ensure high-quality results
quiz.explain: It divides the effort into smaller steps or sub-processes.

quiz.q: What does SDLC stand for?
quiz.explain: The system development life cycle describes the phases of a system's life.

quiz.q: Who originally created Git?
quiz.explain: Linus Torvalds created Git for developing the Linux kernel.

quiz.q: Git is a…
quiz.explain: Git is distributed version control software.

quiz.q: A web application…
quiz.explain: Web apps are built with web technologies and run in the browser.

courses.summary: Understand cloud computing, the DevOps way of working, and how containers package software.

lessons.title: Cloud computing
lessons.why: Most new systems run in the cloud, and cloud skills appear in many tech job posts.
lessons.try: List three services you use every day (email, file storage, video calls) that run in the cloud.

lessons.title: DevOps
lessons.why: DevOps teams release changes faster and more safely by automating builds, tests and deployments.
lessons.try: Name one manual step in your team's work that automation could make faster and more reliable.

lessons.title: Containers with Docker
lessons.why: Containers make software run the same way on a laptop, a server or the cloud.
lessons.try: Install Docker Desktop and run the hello-world container.

quiz.q: Whose definition of cloud computing is quoted in the lesson?
quiz.explain: The lesson quotes the ISO definition.

quiz.q: Cloud computing gives network access to…
options: a scalable, elastic pool of shareable resources provisioned on demand
quiz.explain: That is the ISO definition of cloud computing.

quiz.q: DevOps is…
options: the integration and automation of software development and IT operations
quiz.explain: DevOps integrates and automates development and operations.

quiz.q: Which are generally named as key DevOps principles?
options: Secrecy, manual work and slow feedback
Shared ownership, workflow automation and rapid feedback
quiz.explain: DevOps is generally characterised by shared ownership, automation and rapid feedback.

quiz.q: Docker delivers software in packages called…
quiz.explain: Docker uses OS-level virtualisation to deliver software in containers.

courses.summary: Get comfortable with Linux, the command line and the TCP/IP protocols that connect the internet.

lessons.title: Linux
lessons.why: Linux runs most servers and cloud systems, so it is a core skill for IT, cloud and security jobs.
lessons.try: Try a Linux distribution such as Ubuntu in a virtual machine or a free online terminal.

lessons.title: How the internet connects
lessons.why: Understanding how data travels across networks helps you troubleshoot connections and secure systems.
lessons.try: Run ping to a website from your computer and note how long the replies take.

lessons.title: The command line
lessons.why: The command line lets you control computers quickly and automate tasks, especially on servers without a screen.
lessons.try: Open a terminal and use commands to list files, create a folder and move into it.

quiz.q: Linux is a family of…
options: free and open-source Unix-like operating systems
quiz.explain: Linux is a family of free, open-source Unix-like operating systems.

quiz.q: Who first released the Linux kernel in 1991?
quiz.explain: Linus Torvalds released the Linux kernel on 17 September 1991.

quiz.q: Which are the foundational protocols of the internet protocol suite?
quiz.explain: TCP, UDP and IP are the foundational protocols.

quiz.q: How many abstraction layers does the internet protocol suite use?
quiz.explain: Link, internet, transport and application: four layers.

quiz.q: In a command-line interface you interact with software through…
options: commands typed as lines of text
quiz.explain: Each command is formatted as a line of text.

courses.summary: Learn what cybersecurity protects, how social engineering tricks people, and how teams respond to incidents.

lessons.title: Computer security
lessons.why: As more services go digital, organisations of every size need people who can protect systems and data.
lessons.try: Turn on two-factor authentication for one of your important accounts.

lessons.title: Social engineering
lessons.why: Many attacks target people rather than technology. Recognising pressure tactics is a first line of defence.
lessons.try: Write down how you would check a caller who says they are from your bank and asks for a code.

lessons.title: Handling security incidents
lessons.why: When an attack happens, a clear and practised response limits the damage.
lessons.try: Find out who you should report a suspected security incident to at your workplace.

quiz.q: Computer security protects software, systems and networks from…
options: threats such as unauthorised disclosure, theft or damage
quiz.explain: It protects against unauthorised disclosure, theft, damage and disruption.

quiz.q: Which systems does the lesson call particularly sensitive to security breaches?
options: Power grids, electoral processes and finance
quiz.explain: Systems managing essential services are especially sensitive.

quiz.q: Social engineering uses…
options: psychological pressure to make people act or reveal confidential information
quiz.explain: It manipulates people rather than technology.

quiz.q: Phishing is a type of…
quiz.explain: The lesson states that phishing is a type of social engineering.

quiz.q: The primary purpose of incident management is…
options: a well-understood, predictable response to damaging events and intrusions
quiz.explain: Incident management develops a predictable response, carried out by a response team.

courses.summary: Design products people find easy and useful: UX basics, usability testing and wireframes.

lessons.title: User experience design
lessons.why: Good UX reduces mistakes and support calls and keeps users coming back. It is driven by evidence, not taste.
lessons.try: Use a website or app you dislike and note the three moments where you got stuck.

lessons.title: Usability testing
lessons.why: Watching real users exposes confusing designs before they cost money.
lessons.try: Ask two people to complete one task on a website while thinking aloud, and note where they hesitate.

lessons.title: Wireframes
lessons.why: Wireframes let you agree on layout and priorities quickly, before anyone spends time on visual design or code.
lessons.try: Sketch a wireframe of a simple sign-up page on paper: the fields, the button and the help text.

quiz.q: In UX design, decisions are driven by…
options: research, data analysis and test results
quiz.explain: UX decisions rest on research, data and testing rather than opinions.

quiz.q: How does UX design differ from user interface (UI) design?
options: UX covers the whole perceived experience; UI focuses on the interface itself
UI covers marketing and UX does not
quiz.explain: UI design focuses on the interface; UX covers usability, usefulness, desirability and more.

quiz.q: Usability testing evaluates a product by…
quiz.explain: It gives direct input on how real users use the system.

quiz.q: A website wireframe mainly focuses on…
options: what a screen does — layout, functions and content priority
quiz.explain: Wireframes focus on what a screen does, not what it looks like.

quiz.q: Wireframes can be…
options: pencil sketches or drawings made with software
quiz.explain: They can be pencil drawings, whiteboard sketches or made in software.

courses.summary: Learn how organisations improve and automate processes with BPM, RPA and low-code tools.

lessons.title: Managing business processes
lessons.why: Before automating, understand and improve the process itself — otherwise you only automate the mess.
lessons.try: Draw the steps of one process at work (for example approving an invoice) and mark the slowest step.

lessons.title: Robotic process automation
lessons.why: RPA bots can take over repetitive screen work, such as copying invoice data into a bookkeeping system.
lessons.try: List three repetitive copy-and-paste tasks in your job that a bot could do.

lessons.title: Low-code platforms
lessons.why: Low-code tools let non-programmers build simple apps and workflows, putting automation within reach of many office workers.
lessons.try: Build a simple approval flow in a free low-code or workflow tool.

quiz.q: Business process management (BPM) is the discipline of…
options: discovering, modelling, analysing, improving and automating business processes
quiz.explain: BPM uses various methods to understand and improve processes.

quiz.q: According to the lesson, how does BPM differ from RPA?
options: BPM automates workflows; RPA automates tasks by recording repetitive human activities
RPA is a type of accounting
quiz.explain: Organisations often combine both.

quiz.q: RPA automates tasks using scripts that…
options: mimic human interaction with application user interfaces
quiz.explain: RPA follows a predefined workflow by acting on the user interface.

quiz.q: Which example of RPA does the lesson give?
options: Extracting invoice data from an email and typing it into a bookkeeping system
quiz.explain: RPA can move data between applications, such as from an email into bookkeeping software.

quiz.q: A low-code development platform…
options: lets people build applications with little or no code, often visually
requires writing everything in machine code
quiz.explain: LCDPs usually offer a graphical environment with little coding.

courses.summary: Understand connected devices: the Internet of Things, embedded systems and the sensors behind them.

lessons.title: The Internet of Things
lessons.why: Factories, farms, buildings and fleets are adding connected sensors. IoT skills help turn their data into savings.
lessons.try: List three smart devices around you and the data each one collects.

lessons.title: Embedded systems
lessons.why: Embedded systems are the small dedicated computers inside machines, from washing machines to cars.
lessons.try: Pick one appliance at home and guess which tasks its embedded computer controls.

lessons.title: Sensors
lessons.why: Sensors are the starting point of any IoT system: they turn real-world changes into data.
lessons.try: Name a sensor that could help save energy in your workplace and what it would measure.

quiz.q: The Internet of Things describes…
options: physical objects with sensors and software that exchange data over networks
quiz.explain: IoT devices are embedded with sensors, processing and software that exchange data.

quiz.q: According to the lesson, what is the largest single application of IoT?
options: Commercial asset tracking and fleet management
quiz.explain: Asset tracking and fleet management account for about 22% of the IoT market.

quiz.q: An embedded system is…
options: a specialised computer system with a dedicated function inside a larger device
quiz.explain: It is embedded as part of a complete device.

quiz.q: Modern embedded systems are often based on…
quiz.explain: Microcontrollers combine a processor with memory and peripheral interfaces.

quiz.q: A sensor is a device that…
options: detects events or changes in its environment and sends the information to other electronics
quiz.explain: Sensors convert a sensed quantity into a signal for other electronics.

courses.summary: Promote products online: digital marketing channels, search engine optimisation and web analytics.

lessons.title: Digital marketing
lessons.why: Small businesses increasingly sell online. Digital marketing skills help them reach customers at low cost.
lessons.try: Pick a local business and list three digital channels it could use to reach new customers.

lessons.title: Search engine optimisation
lessons.why: Appearing in search results brings visitors who are already looking for what you offer, without paying for every click.
lessons.try: Search for a product your organisation offers and note which competitors appear first, and why.

lessons.title: Measuring with web analytics
lessons.why: Analytics shows which campaigns actually bring visitors and customers, so the budget goes to what works.
lessons.try: Open a free web analytics demo account and find the number of visitors and page views for last week.

quiz.q: Digital marketing uses…
options: digital technologies and media platforms to promote products and services
quiz.explain: It promotes products through computers, phones and other digital media.

quiz.q: Which is a digital marketing method listed in the lesson?
quiz.explain: SEO is one of the methods listed.

quiz.q: SEO focuses on increasing traffic from…
quiz.explain: SEO targets organic search traffic rather than paid advertising.

quiz.q: Web analytics is…
options: the measurement, collection, analysis and reporting of web data
quiz.explain: Web analytics measures and reports web data to optimise web use.

quiz.q: Which information does web analytics typically provide?
options: The number of visitors and page views
quiz.explain: It reports visitors, page views and behaviour profiles.
